A rider's critical power and W'

Source: R/cp.R
zv_rider_cp.Rd

Looks up a rider's most recent critical power (CP, W) and W' (J) as modelled by ZwiftRacing.app, or estimates them from ZwiftPower's 90-day power curve when ZwiftRacing has nothing recent enough.

Usage

zv_rider_cp(
  zr,
  zp,
  zwift_id,
  max_age_days = 90,
  durations = c(120, 1200),
  tries = 3
)

Arguments

zr

A zr_client(), or NULL to skip ZwiftRacing.app.

zp

A zp_session(), or NULL to skip the ZwiftPower fallback.

zwift_id

Zwift rider id.

max_age_days

ZwiftRacing values older than this are ignored. At most 365.

durations

Range of durations (seconds) used for the ZwiftPower fit.

tries

How many of the rider's most recent ZwiftRacing events to try.

Value

A one-row tibble: zwid, cp (W), w_prime (J), source ("zwiftracing", "zwiftpower_fit", or NA if neither worked), as_of (POSIXct: the event, or the newest effort in the fit), age_days, event_id (the ZwiftRacing event the values come from) and fit_r2 (R² of the ZwiftPower fit; NA for ZwiftRacing values).

Details

ZwiftRacing.app. CP and W' are only published inside event results, as each rider's power.CP and power.AWC at the time of the event. The function finds the rider's races from the last max_age_days and reads their row from the newest event that has them (trying up to tries events). A service key lists those races from ZwiftRacing; a user (Hobby) key has no such route, so they come from the rider's ZwiftPower race history, and zp is needed for this step too. If the key has no allowance for event results, the function warns (now and then, not for every rider) and uses the ZwiftPower fit.

ZwiftPower fallback. If ZwiftRacing has no result within max_age_days, or zr is NULL, the two-parameter model P(t) = CP + W'/t is fitted to the 90-day curve from zp_power_curve() by linear regression of work on time (P*t = W' + CP*t) over the durations range (default 2-20 minutes). The fit is only as good as the efforts behind the curve: a rider who has not gone full gas for 2 and 20 minutes lately will get a low CP and an unreliable W'.

A rider or event the API doesn't know (HTTP 404) just moves on to the next source. Any other error, such as a rejected key, is raised.

See also

zv_signups_cp() for every rider signed up to a race.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
zr <- zr_client()
zp <- zp_set_cookie(zp_session(), Sys.getenv("ZP_SID"))
zv_rider_cp(zr, zp, 1234567)
zv_rider_cp(NULL, zp, 1234567)        # ZwiftPower fit only
} # }
